newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds were dragged lower by pre-weekend profit-taking in bund futures whjich wiped out gains posted in the morning.

Yield spreads versus Germany narrowed a little further following Thursday's 20-basis-point hike in the Dutch central bank's special advances rate which was widely seen as a measure to counter recent guilder weakness against the German mark.
The Dutch government's February 2002 bond yielded three basis points below the January 2002 bund compared with seven basis points below on Wednesday, the day before the hike.
The February 2007 benchmark yielded eight basis points below the January 2007 bund versus -11 basis points midweek.
Economists said the guilder's recent slide against the mark flowed from a variety of factors including a big gap between the special advances rate and Germany's equivalent, the repo rate.

The Dutch central bank has a long-standing policy of pegging the guilder tightly to the mark. But despite the rate hike, the mark was trading at 1.1248 guilders late on Friday compared with 1.1215 a week earlier and a low of 1.1160 last May.
The rate hike lifted the Dutch special advances rate to 2.70 percent, still 30 basis points below the repo rate of 3.00 pct.
Economists said the Dutch rate hike was not aimed at taming inflation which is running at an annual rate of 2.3 percent in January, compared with 1.8 percent in Germany.
Dutch inflation, though higher than in Germany, was still far from excessive and was consistent with the faster growth of the Dutch economy, they said.
